title: LTX Desktop on a 24 GB Mac: Stopped at Setup, Below the Vendor's Memory Floor
dek: Hands-on test on a 24 GB Mac. The app launched smoothly, then the setup screen asked for 129.1 GB of model downloads and the tester gave up: 24 GB of memory is not enough for this app, he says.

seo.title: LTX Desktop Hands-on Test: Stopped at Setup on a 24 GB Mac
seo.description: Hands-on test of LTX Desktop on a 24 GB Mac: setup asked for 129.1 GB of models, the vendor's memory floor is higher, and the test ended there.

faq: Can a Mac with 24 GB run LTX Desktop?

The tester stopped at the setup screen and concluded that his 24 GB Mac cannot run it. The test never reached generation. Lightricks' README lists a floor of 32 GiB total RAM for local generation on macOS.
How much disk space does LTX Desktop need?
The setup screen listed five model downloads totalling 129.1 GB, and the test Mac showed 32.9 GB available. The README asks for 100 GB or more of free disk space, and up to 160 GB with LoRAs.
How big is the LTX Desktop installer?
About 700 MB, as read by the tester. The models are downloaded separately during setup and are far larger.
Do I need a Hugging Face account for LTX Desktop?
The setup screen asks the user to sign in to Hugging Face and accept a license to download gated models. The test stopped before sign-in.
What does LTX Desktop download during setup?

Five items: LTX 2.5 (41.5 GB), a Gemma 4 text encoder with LTX 2.5 projections (24.5 GB), a Gemma 4 E2B instruct prompt enhancer (9.6 GB), the Z-Image-Turbo text-to-image model (28.9 GB) and LoRAs (24.6 GB).

verdict.general: Not scored: the test ended at the setup screen, before any video or image was made. What the notes and screenshots show: a smooth first launch, a required Hugging Face sign-in, and a model list that totals 129.1 GB against 32.9 GB of free space. The tester's conclusion is that his 24 GB of unified memory is not enough to run the app, not that disk space is the problem. The vendor's README points the same way: it lists 32 GiB of total RAM as the floor for local generation on a Mac.
verdict.fit: Not a fit for this machine, per the tester. The largest single download (LTX 2.5, 41.5 GB) is bigger than the 24 GB of memory, although download size is not the same as memory needed at run time (assumption). The README, read on 20 October 2026, says Macs below 24 GB use the cloud API only and that 32 GB is limited to 540p and 5 s; 48 GB or more is listed for full local generation. The app nevertheless offered the local model download on this 24 GB Mac, which the README does not explain (see 'How the test went').

chapters.title: Installer
items: The installer is a file of about 700 MB.
Where it was downloaded from is not in the notes.

chapters.title: First launch
items: The app opens to a splash screen: 'LTX Desktop', a loading bar, and '© 2026 Lightricks' at the bottom.

chapters.title: Setup screen
items: The Setup screen has a 'Hugging Face access' box: 'Sign in and accept the license to download gated models.' with a Sign in button. The tester did not sign in.

Under 'Model downloads' five items are ticked: LTX 2.5 (41.5 GB), Gemma 4 text encoder with LTX 2.5 projections (24.5 GB), Gemma 4 E2B instruct prompt enhancer, folder (9.6 GB), Z-Image-Turbo model for text-to-image generation (28.9 GB) and LoRAs (24.6 GB). The screen shows 'Total: 129.1 GB'.
The models folder is /Users/hanskuepper/Library/Application Support/LTXDesktop/models, with '32.9 GB available'. The folder can be changed with a Change button.
129.1 GB is more than 32.9 GB by 96.2 GB. Whether the app blocks the download, warns, or lets it fail part-way was not tested.

chapters.title: Why the test stopped
items: 'And that ended. I cannot run this on my little laptop.'
The tester's reason is memory: his Mac has 24 GB of unified memory, and he considers that too little for this app. Freeing disk space would not change that, he says.

The largest single download (LTX 2.5, 41.5 GB) is bigger than 24 GB. Download size is not the same as memory needed while running, because an app can load or compress weights in parts; no memory reading was taken.
No download was started, no generation was attempted, and no memory warning appears in either screenshot.

chapters.title: What the vendor says (read 20 October 2026)
items: The GitHub README (Lightricks/LTX-Desktop) lists for macOS: Apple Silicon (M1 or later) with 48 GB or more for full local generation; 32 GB limited to 540p and 5 s; less than 24 GB and Intel Macs use the Gen Space API only. The app needs macOS 14 or later.

The README also states floors of 32 GiB total RAM and macOS 26 or later for local generation on a Mac; below them the app shows a 'Coming soon to your device' notice instead of the generation tools. All platforms need 100 GB or more of free disk space, up to 160 GB or more with LoRAs. An LTX API key is never required to start.

The test Mac has 24 GB, below the README's 32 GiB floor, yet the app showed the local model download and no 'Coming soon' notice in the screenshots. The macOS version and the app version were not recorded, so the two cannot be compared.

Search results also surfaced older Lightricks help-center pages. As summarised, they say that on a Mac generation goes through the LTX API, that local inference on Mac is not yet supported, and that 16 GB or more of unified memory is needed. The help-center page itself returned an error when opened, so this is second-hand and may be out of date.
The README and the screenshots may describe different app versions. Which statement applies to the tester's build is unknown.

claims: The five listed sizes add up to 129.1 GB, matching the total shown.
100 GB or more of free disk space needed; up to 160 GB or more with LoRAs
The setup screen's total (129.1 GB) sits inside that range. Disk space was not the tester's stated reason for stopping.
Local generation on a Mac needs 32 GiB total RAM; 48 GB or more for full local generation; less than 24 GB uses the cloud API only
Not tested. The test Mac has 24 GB. The app still showed the local model download.
On macOS, generation goes through the LTX API; local inference is not supported
Contradicted by the setup screen, which offers local model downloads. Possibly a different app version.
Fewer than 10-15% of MacBook users have 32 GB or more of memory; fewer than 3-5% have 64 GB or more; fewer than 1-2% of Windows machines have 64 GB or more
No study, publisher or date is given. Not checked here.

background_intro: Not hands-on. The items below come from the splash screen, the vendor's GitHub README and the tester's notes. The README was read on 20 October 2026 with a web-fetch tool that summarises pages, and was not independently verified.
background: The splash screen names Lightricks as the maker ('© 2026 Lightricks').
The README is the vendor's own project page for LTX Desktop on GitHub (Lightricks/LTX-Desktop). It states the system floors and disk needs summarised under 'What the vendor says'.
Older help-center pages surfaced by a web search describe Mac generation as API only; they were not opened (the page returned an error) and may be out of date.
The memory-tier statistics in the tester's notes are credited to 'Google' without a source.
